title: Peshawar joins the kingdom
hookLine: the frontier city is brought into the kingdom

lines: A CITY AT THE MOUTH OF A PASS.
A DOOR, NOT JUST A CITY.
cards: Peshawar is a market town where the plains run out. Caravans unload in its bazaars: horses, dried fruit, carpets from beyond the hills. Behind the city, the road climbs west toward Afghanistan.
Traders came down that road. Armies came down it too, again and again, into the Punjab. A city at the mouth of a pass like that is never just a city.
It's a door, and whoever holds it decides who comes in.

teach.h: YEARS OF PULL BETWEEN TWO POWERS.
teach.b: Peshawar didn't fall in a day. For years it sat between the Sikh kingdom and the Afghan rulers, paying tribute to Lahore at times, slipping back at others.
Sikh histories tell of battles on the plains around it and the slow pull of the city toward Lahore. Then the general.

teach.h: HARI SINGH NALWA BRINGS IT IN.
teach.b: You met him a few days ago: Hari Singh Nalwa, who held the frontier. As Sikh histories tell it, he brought Peshawar fully into the kingdom and then governed the region.
He built forts, among them Jamrud near the pass, where he would later fall. With Peshawar held, the kingdom's edge sat at the foot of the Khyber.

teach.h: A SIKH GUARD ON THE INVADERS' ROAD.
teach.b: The door armies had used to come down into the Punjab was now held from Lahore, and Sikh tradition remembers it with pride: the invaders' road now had a Sikh guard on it. But a border city is never quiet.
Peshawar had its own Pashtun leaders with their own loyalties, and the Afghan rulers wanted it back. Holding it meant troops, forts and constant watch.

teach.h: AN EDGE IS STRONG AND EXPOSED.
teach.b: An edge is where a kingdom stands guard, and where it can be struck, both at once.
A fort at the mouth of a pass, its gate facing the hills: that's the edge.

how: Sikhs remember Peshawar in histories of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's reign and in the stories of Hari Singh Nalwa, the general who held the north-west frontier.

o: a river fort the Maharaja built on the Sutlej
a frontier city at the mouth of the Khyber Pass
a market town on the road from Lahore to Delhi

games.q: the frontier city — tap the pairs.
p: the gap in the hills toward Afghanistan

games.q: you hold the city at the mouth of the pass. the old rulers want it back. what does holding it take?
o: a single treaty and then peace.
giving the pass away to keep the city.
games.why: Hari Singh Nalwa built forts, Jamrud among them, and kept watch. an edge is never quiet.

practice: Think of the edges of your own world: the last street you know well, the far side of your circle, the subject you always avoid.
Pick one, rest your attention there for a few breaths without pushing past it, and notice how it feels to stand at the line. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Peshawar, the city at the mouth of the Khyber, pulled toward Lahore for years and brought into the kingdom under Hari Singh Nalwa.
